title: Front and rear platform wording
wording: Front ride-height platform helps define diffuser feed. Rear ride-height platform helps define diffuser expansion/outlet and scrape/choke behavior. Diffuser metrics are derived geometry proxies, not measured downforce.

title: CFS and front feed matter
wording: CFS/front feed evidence matters when interpreting Next Gen platform complaints.
do_not_say: rear ride height explains the whole aero state

title: Rear height is not alone
wording: Rear height alone does not determine rear aero behavior; inspect it with front feed, outlet proxy, scrape, and speed loss.
do_not_say: rear height alone proves the aero result

title: Front higher is contextual
wording: A front platform that is higher than the rear is not automatically wrong; the useful question is whether the feed, scrape margin, and speed trend agree.
do_not_say: front higher than rear is automatically wrong

title: Lower is contextual
wording: Lower is not automatically faster if it creates contact, unstable feed, or speed loss.

title: Proxy is not downforce
wording: Diffuser proxy channels are geometry-derived indicators for comparison and are not a force measurement.

title: Inspect combined platform
wording: Inspect CFS/front height, rear platform, diffuser proxy, scrape, and speed loss together before naming a platform direction.
do_not_say: one channel proves the platform answer
